title: Evaluate output-weighted per-token floor + enterprise SQ response alignment
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Run a controlled experiment to test an output-weighted per-token pricing model combined with a minimum per-request streaming floor, and prepare canonical language and data for enterprise security questionnaire (SQ) and contract exhibits. Goal: measure revenue delta, developer friction, and customer objections for per-output-unit billing vs symmetric IO billing; produce recommended contract language and pricing exhibits for sales/legal.
background: Current hosted pricing is primarily symmetric input/output token rates with streaming as a discounted add-on. Sales and some enterprise customers have requested clearer cost predictability on streaming-heavy workloads (e.g., embeddings + long-form generation) and explicit contract exhibits for minimums. Engineering has suggested that output token work is more expensive on average due to decoding and post-processing, so an asymmetric rate may better reflect unit economics. This ticket formalizes a probe to test that hypothesis and align legal/Sales on SQ responses.
hypothesis: Charging a higher per-output-token rate plus a small per-streaming-request floor (to cover setup and streaming overhead) will increase margin on generative workloads by ~6-12% while keeping churn < 4% among pilot customers; enterprise SQ/update materials can be standardized into two optional exhibits (streaming floor exhibit and IO split exhibit).
acceptance_criteria: Run pricing simulation across last 90 days of hosted traffic and produce delta report
Deploy experiment to 3 pilot orgs (one AI-native startup, one mid-market SaaS, one enterprise) with opt-in billing flags
Produce canonical SQ language and two contract exhibit templates (streaming-floor, io-split) reviewed by Legal
Present results and recommendation to GTM and Exec with clear rollout decision (A/B expand, iterate, or abandon)
tasks: Model economic impact by model family and sequence length distribution
Design experiment flags and opt-in UI for pilot customers
Create contract exhibit drafts with Legal and Sales sequences
Instrument billing pipeline to emit per-request IO split and streaming-floor charges in test mode
Prepare customer communication and error fallback for unexpected bill spikes
